one_month_reasoning: The scheduled event in the window is ASML's Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-14 [15]. Q3 guidance was EUR 11-12B at a 55-57% gross margin, and the consensus is EUR 10.65 EPS on EUR 11.68B, inside the guide. Hitting the FY26 midpoint needs about EUR 14.4B in Q4 [1], so the Q4 guide and the first 2027 framing (capacity about 85 low-NA EUV, 'nearly sold out') drive the reaction. A late-October FOMC meeting is also in the window, but after the 09-16 hike [30] markets lean towards no change in October, so it is a small risk. The MATCH Act cannot move inside the window: the Senate is out until about 11-09 and conference is expected in December. Upside: Micron's record print on 10-01 (FY27 capex above FY26) [23], and TrendForce still has 4Q26 conventional DRAM contracts up 10-15% [11,31]. Downside: the stock has already rebounded about 15% from the real September low close of $1,575.15 on 09-14 [27] (my round-1 '$1,390' was wrong, so less recovery is priced in than I claimed, and that removes most of the reversal argument), and pre-print commentary talks of cautious Q3 expectations [33]. I do not treat the Substack 'lower highs' read as a signal. With no edge on the print, I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred at $1,815 (a very small tilt from the Micron read-through) with a 13.5% monthly sigma (46%/3.5 = 13.1%, nudged up for the earnings event).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (70%) and FCF yield (30%) on what the market will treat as NTM in Oct 2027, i.e. FY2028, converted at spot EUR/USD 1.1243. FY28 EPS of EUR 61 x 27.5x x 1.1243 = $1,886. FY28 FCF/share of about EUR 48.9 at a 2.9% yield x 1.1243 = $1,897. Blended: about $1,890.

bear.story: Conventional DRAM contract growth keeps slowing (from +58-63% in Q2 to +10-15% in 4Q26) and turns negative in 2027, and memory customers push out 2028 tools. A December NDAA conference keeps the MATCH Act, which ends DUV sales and servicing at the named Chinese fabs (China about 20% of FY26 sales). The 2028 capacity step is shelved, a second Fed hike compresses multiples, and the receivables build does not reverse. FY28 EPS stalls near EUR 50 at about 20x x 1.1243: about $1,125.

base.story: Low-NA EUV goes from 65 to about 85 in 2027, and 2027 is nearly sold out. Memory fabs ramp from H2 2027, and TSMC capex (US$60-64B in 2026) holds or rises in 2027. FY28 revenue lands near the EUR 65B consensus, and EPS reaches about EUR 61 after a MATCH haircut. China fades but is not banned, and the multiple de-rates to 27.5x under tighter rates: about $1,890.

bull.story: The 2028 capacity step goes ahead, High-NA adoption broadens (Samsung/SK hynix DRAM in 2028), TSMC raises 2027 capex again, memory profits do not peak before late 2027, and the MATCH Act is dropped in conference. FY28 EPS reaches about EUR 70 (near the MarketScreener EUR 68 consensus) at about 33x x 1.1243: about $2,600. I trimmed this from $2,700 for the Fed hike and FX.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $1,150 (about 36% under spot and about 27% under the real September 2026 low close of $1,575.15 on 09-14), the market would be pricing about 20x on flat FY28 EPS of about EUR 51 at EUR/USD 1.1243. A drop that far below the recent low most likely means a fundamental break, such as a memory capex reversal with 2027-28 tool pushouts, an enacted China DUV/servicing ban, a shelved 2028 capacity step, or a guidance cut, rather than ordinary 46%-vol noise. I keep $1,150 rather than the supervisor's $1,200 because a 20-25% sell-off on rates alone (as in September) can take the stock into the $1,200s without a fundamental break.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's fact-checks, which I verified myself, change three of my inputs. (1) FX: EUR/USD closed at 1.12428 on 10-01 [28], not 1.1355, which takes about 1% off every USD value. (2) The September low: the low close was $1,575.15 on 09-14 (intraday $1,572.84) [27]. My '$1,390' was wrong, so the rebound is +15%, not +30%, and the thesis-break and 1-month narratives are re-based. (3) Rates: the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 09-16 and most participants expect another hike [30], so I trim the horizon multiple from 28x to 27.5x and lift the FCF yield from 2.85% to 2.9%. I also now anchor FY28 to the checkable consensus revenue of EUR 65.0B [29] instead of my own EUR 64B. At about a 36% net margin on 372M shares that gives about EUR 62.9, which I cut about 3% for MATCH risk and DRAM deceleration to EUR 61. I do not adopt MarketScreener's EUR 68.3, because it implies a share count of about 357M. As the supervisor asked, I down-weight the single-Substack inputs: Koh's 110+ 2028 units and 'lower highs', Glassdoor hiring, and GTOAI's TSMC US$60-110B are replaced or demoted. TSMC's own 6-K shows 2026 capex raised to US$60-64B [32], which is the checkable bull signal. Luminix's '+0-5% 4Q26' conflicts with TrendForce's +10-15% [11,31], so it is a watch item. The deceleration itself is real, though, and keeps the bear case at 20%. Results: fair value $1,890 (from $1,955). Scenarios are $1,125 / $1,890 / $2,600 at 20/54/26% (probability-weighted about $1,920). The 12-month ladder is a mixture of 85% lognormal (median $1,890, sigma 0.40) and 15% bear lognormal (median $1,175, sigma 0.35), with the $452 strike held at 0.997 for the Taiwan/geopolitical tail. That gives P(>= spot) of 0.48. The 1-month ladder is a lognormal at $1,815 with a 13.5% sigma. Research was limited to about 8 follow-up queries. X/Twitter remained unreachable.
